# KV Cache: Enabling Efficient Long-Context Inference

## The Memory Problem in Autoregressive Generation

When transformer models generate text, they process tokens sequentially—each new token depends on all previous tokens in the sequence. In naive implementation, this means recomputing the same key and value projections for every position at every decoding step. For a sequence of length n generating n tokens, this results in O(n²) total computation, with redundant work growing quadratically as context length increases.

KV cache addresses this inefficiency by storing computed keys and values once and reusing them across subsequent generation steps. Instead of recalculating attention projections for the entire prefix each time a new token is produced, the model computes keys and values for new tokens only, appending them to persistent caches that persist throughout the inference session.

## Technical Mechanism

During each forward pass, the transformer computes query, key, and value matrices through linear projections on token embeddings. With KV caching enabled, after the initial prefill phase processes the full prompt, subsequent decoding steps compute queries only for the newly generated token while retrieving cached keys and values for all prior positions. The attention operation then combines fresh queries with the accumulated key-value pairs, producing outputs without reprocessing historical tokens.

This reduces per-token inference cost from O(n) to O(1) with respect to context length, transforming the total cost of generating a sequence of n tokens from O(n²) to O(n). The memory overhead grows linearly with context size, requiring storage proportional to batch size multiplied by number of layers, attention heads, head dimension, and sequence length.
